text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Diagnostic workup: spirometry before and after bronchodilator, FeNO, DLCO, blood count with eosinophils, total IgE, alpha-1 antitrypsin, NT-proBNP, interferon-gamma release assay, chest X-ray, and CT of the chest if airflow limitation persists after bronchodilator; albuterol withheld for 6 hours before testing
  • Exposure reduction from today: no open coal or wood fires in his rooms (electric or heat-pump heating instead); a portable HEPA air cleaner sized for his study and bedroom; daily check of the air quality index, with city trips and outdoor exertion avoided on alert days; a well-fitted N95 respirator on unavoidable high-pollution days; quieter routes away from main roads
  • Pulmonology consultation on the diagnosis (asthma, COPD, or both), the need for CT, treatment, and pulmonary rehabilitation
  • Shared decision on treatment: budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 mcg as maintenance and reliever, two inhalations twice daily plus one as needed, no more than 12 a day; albuterol stopped; inhaler technique taught and checked at every visit; a written asthma action plan
  • Pulmonary rehabilitation: an eight-week, twice-weekly program of supervised exercise training and education, with a six-minute walk test before and after
  • Vaccinations: pneumococcal conjugate vaccine PCV20 at the diagnosis visit; influenza, COVID-19, and RSV vaccines in the autumn; recombinant zoster vaccine
  • Monitoring: Asthma Control Test, inhaler technique, adherence, reliever use, and exposures at every visit; spirometry and FeNO 3 months after starting treatment, then every 1 to 2 years; home peak flow diary
  • Add-on tiotropium 2.5 mcg soft-mist inhaler, two inhalations once daily, for persistent symptoms and airflow limitation on medium-dose budesonide-formoterol; written action plan updated with peak-flow zones from his personal best of 440 L/min
  • After any flare: a review within one week, booked by the clinic when he calls or is seen for the flare

resource.title: John Locke synthetic care plan
resource.description: Evaluate a 59-year-old never-smoker with a lifelong cough, wheeze, and breathlessness, worse in city air and by open fires at home: pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry interpreted with race-neutral GLI equations and the ATS/ERS 2022 bronchodilator criterion, FeNO, blood eosinophils and IgE, DLCO, alpha-1 antitrypsin, NT-proBNP, an interferon-gamma release assay, chest X-ray, and CT for persistent airflow limitation; a reasoned decision between asthma with persistent airflow limitation and COPD from non-tobacco exposures (GINA 2025, GOLD 2025); GINA track 1 budesonide-formoterol maintenance-and-reliever therapy with add-on tiotropium; inhaler technique, adherence, and a written action plan with peak-flow zones; pulmonary rehabilitation; air pollution as a cause and exposure reduction (WHO 2021 air quality guidelines, air quality alerts, removing indoor solid-fuel smoke, HEPA air cleaning, respirators on unavoidable high-pollution days); vaccinations; and management of a viral flare by the action plan (CMID asthma and COPD monographs).
